PullRequest.Title: mcp: Show non-migratable servers
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- list MCP servers that cannot be migrated alongside eligible servers, with explicit migratable/not-migratable counts
- provide source navigation, MCP details navigation, and an Edit Configuration action that selects the server JSON
- surface explicit `cwd`, SSE transport, and version metadata as partially supported with migration guidance
- allow disabled MCP servers to migrate while preserving their disabled state on the root-server identity
- preserve migration exclusion reasons through the shared migration service and accessible view

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint on `aiCustomizationManagement.css`
- focused MCP support, migration planner, migration service, management editor, and root discovery tests
- manually verified migration inventory, partial-support badges and diagnostics, MCP details navigation, source navigation, and configuration selection in Code OSS

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed predicate, the planner call path, the per-source deduplication, and the sequential await are explicit. Remote/agent-host roots are covered by this subsystem and its tests; only the exact number and latency of affected workspace roots varies by user.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem-provider reads of distinct workspace .vscode/mcp.json files, including remote/agent-host provider calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of distinct workspace roots whose MCP inventory contains only partially supported servers. Reads are deduplicated per source URI, but createPlan awaits the first read for each source inside the server loop, so effective concurrency is one and latency sums across roots.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased migration-dashboard latency and repeated remote filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The prior compatibility.kind === 'supported' gate rejected every partially supported server before source-file validation, so roots containing only these servers caused no planner filesystem read.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Partially supported servers (including the newly classified cwd, version, and SSE cases) now enter the planner's source-validation path. For each distinct source URI, createPlan starts readMcpServers and immediately awaits it before advancing to the next root.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 61 newly lets compatibility.kind === 'partiallySupported' pass isMcpServerMigrationDeliverable. Those servers now proceed to sourceServers/readMcpServers in createPlan; previously the supported-only predicate excluded them before any file read.
Findings.Title: Short-circuit partial servers before reading each workspace config
Findings.Impact: With migration enabled, opening the AI Customizations editor or receiving an MCP refresh in a multi-root remote workspace can block the inventory on the sum of one remote read per affected root, even though these partial servers are ultimately listed as not migratable. Ten or more roots can turn provider round-trip latency into a noticeable wait on every refresh.
Findings.Evidence: createPlan calls isMcpServerMigrationDeliverable before source access, then caches one readMcpServers promise per sourceUri but immediately awaits it in the same loop. The added predicate therefore creates one serial read per newly admitted source file. CustomizationMigrationService.computeMcpServerMigration awaits createPlan before returning inventory, and the management editor invokes it on initial load and MCP/workbench changes. Tests in customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts explicitly exercise vscode-remote and agent-host URI providers, proving these reads can cross a remote filesystem boundary.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the exclusion listing but classify known partially supported/non-portable servers into exclusions before readMcpServers. If source validation is genuinely required for some partial reason, pre-group those source URIs and read them with a small shared concurrency limit rather than serially in the server loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the AI Customizations migration inventory with MCP migration enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor waits for the MCP support scope to settle and then awaits createPlan before publishing candidates/exclusions and rendering the dashboard. Source-file validation is therefore on the visible inventory's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse each relevant workspace .vscode/mcp.json through IFileService, including vscode-remote/agent-host providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per distinct source URI in an invocation; same-file servers are grouped, but different workspace roots are read serially. The diff newly includes roots represented only by partially supported servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Partially supported servers failed the supported-only gate before source access; fully supported roots were already read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads must complete before computeMcpServerMigration returns inventory to the editor.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct workspace roots/source .vscode/mcp.json files after per-URI deduplication, plus servers per file for in-memory normalization. The changed predicate adds partial-only roots to the effective file-read cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Support updates are debounced by the scope, while editor refreshes cancel superseded requests. Within one createPlan invocation, distinct source-file reads are effectively serialized because each newly created promise is immediately awaited in the server loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The plan caches each source URI only for the lifetime of one invocation. There is no warm cache or coalescing across editor/MCP refreshes; failures and successful reads are retried on the next refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the widened predicate, invocation path, per-source deduplication, immediate await, and remote-provider reachability are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of partial-only roots and remote-provider round-trip time varies, but multi-root remote workspaces make additive latency realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: newly admitted partial servers cause serial per-root filesystem reads on each inventory refresh, even when they are ultimately excluded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and navigate the migratable/not-migratable MCP inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After planning completes, the page synchronously rebuilds migration DOM. Migratable candidates use WorkbenchList virtualization; exclusions are eagerly rendered as rows with buttons, listeners, and managed hovers.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of MCP exclusions across active workspace roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render; no asynchronous fan-out during row creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retained row cache; migrationPageDisposables and the container are cleared and rebuilt on refresh, preventing unbounded retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for eager DOM creation and cleanup; low for material impact at realistic MCP counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large MCP inventories are possible but normally much smaller than file-customization inventories; no concrete realistic cardinality establishes user-visible jank from the eager exclusion rows alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: lifecycle cleanup is present and realistic exclusion cardinality does not establish a high-confidence rendering regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open MCP details and use Edit Configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening details loads the source definition through IFileService. The explicit Edit Configuration action reads the source again only when no source range is available, parses JSON, computes a range, then opens the editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected MCP configuration source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read on detail load and at most one additional read per explicit Edit Configuration click when source.range is absent
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Detail loading already read the source; the additional read/navigation path did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detail content waits for the first read; editor navigation waits for the optional second read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size of the single selected MCP configuration file; work does not scale across the inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One user-selected file operation at a time; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The displayed definition/model is retained only for the current detail and disposed/replaced through existing disposables. The edit action does not cache parsed content.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration files can vary in size, but this is a deliberate single-file user action rather than a hot or scaling path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded, user-initiated single-file work with no repeated collection fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Migrate selected MCP servers, including disabled servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action revalidates support and the plan, performs grouped source/target filesystem transactions, then preserves disabled enablement state before returning completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, verify, and write grouped .vscode/mcp.json and .mcp.json files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped per distinct source/target root rather than per server; disabled servers newly become eligible but share their root transaction with other selected servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled servers were rejected before migration; enabled selected servers already used the same grouped transaction path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected groups complete before the migration result is shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist target disabled state and remove old identity from MCP enablement storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two logical enablement mutations per successfully migrated disabled server
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled servers were not migrated, so their enablement identity was not transferred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after file migration and before returning the result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected candidates grouped by distinct source/target root pairs; disabled-state updates scale with successfully migrated disabled candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration groups execute sequentially to preserve guarded file-update semantics. Enablement updates are synchronous per disabled candidate.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Planning deduplicates source reads only within the invocation. Migration performs fresh reads for correctness; enablement state is persisted in profile/workspace mementos.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed path and grouping.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users generally migrate a small number of MCP servers; the per-server storage mutations do not establish a material regression at realistic counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: filesystem work remains grouped by root and the new state transfer is necessary, bounded to an explicit migration action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show MCP compatibility badges/details and propagate server version metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the experimental migration setting is enabled and the MCP list/detail is visible, a ref-counted support scope computes compatibility from discovered definitions. Version is passed through existing discovery/serialization paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Discovered MCP server definitions in the active scope.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Support recomputation is debounced; visible consumers share ref-counted scope state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scopes are acquired only while visible and disposed on hide/setting disable. Serialized definitions reuse existing discovery lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Compatibility assessment cost scales linearly with server definitions but the diff adds constant-field checks only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the setting now avoids support-scope work when disabled, and version propagation does not add boundary calls or materially change payload scale.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 24 changed files and relevant callers. One medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout issue was submitted for serial remote-capable source reads newly triggered by partially supported servers; eager UI, detail navigation, migration execution, enablement persistence, scope cleanup, and serialization changes did not meet the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
